interpretation
Capex rises materially from original budgets as delivery/demand changes. FY2025 actual was 21.93% above initial ~$75bn and inside final $91–93bn range. This supports capacity-demand visibility but warns against fixed reinvestment forecasts. No revenue forecasting hit-rate or CEO score can be inferred.

accounting model requirements
accounting model requirements · 6 records
  1. Forecast physical capex, depreciation, lease additions/payments, inventory and working capital separately in early years; revenue-change/sales-capital is a compressed proxy.
  2. Keep SBC in operating costs; do not add it back without an explicit offset for equity issued to employees.
  3. Separate cash-flow tax benefits of accelerated depreciation from normalized accrual tax; no terminal tax holiday.
  4. Do not capitalize unrealized equity gains or energy derivative gains as operating earnings.
  5. Satisfy terminal identity: terminal sales/capital = ROIC / after-tax operating margin.
  6. Uncommenced leases and purchase commitments are not automatically additional net debt if already included in cash-flow forecasts.
unresolved gaps
unresolved gaps · 3 records
  1. No refreshed October17 balance sheet; use June30 anchor or explicitly bridge subsequently disclosed financing/investment events.
  2. No independent fair-value appraisal of private equity, customer-credit exposures, pending acquisitions or derivatives.
  3. No credible terminal customer-concentration or AI pricing dataset; scenario stresses remain wide.
invalidation checks
invalidation checks · 5 records
  1. Search growth drops below mid-single digits while AI costs and TAC increase.
  2. Backlog conversion materially misses the disclosed timing of just over 50% over 24 months.
  3. TPU hardware creates worse margins, inventory needs or customer acceptance delays than modeled.
  4. Significantly higher 2027 capex fails to convert into operating cash flow or requires repeated dilutive funding.
  5. Regulatory remedies or competition impair Search distribution and ad monetization.

bounded Model Gaps
bounded Model Gaps · 9 records
  1. Valuation-date stub and post-anchor cash/claims/share roll-forward not integrated; this is a forecast-origin operating EV, not October 17 equity value.
  2. No probability weighting or share-price calibration. Source forecast assumptions are judgments, not reported facts.
  3. Enterprise-to-equity bridge is not computed here; consult the company-specific claim register for resolved evidence, assumptions and remaining uncertainties. Zero is not evidence of absence.
  4. Integrate D&A, TPU hardware inventory/COGS, energy and third-party capacity costs with EBIT before treating overlay as a fully integrated forecast.
  5. Resolve source definition/roll-forward of finance-lease prepayments and capitalized interest, avoiding double deduction.
  6. Use actual stock-award cash payments, not equity-statement withholding amount. ATM proceeds stay zero until issuance is scheduled and dilution modeled.
  7. Tax timing and financing costs are bounded analyst budgets, not group cash tax guidance.
  8. Private-customer funding, customer collections and acquired investment assets each enter once;20,000contingent funding is inside21,900VIE commitments.
  9. Legacy end-of-explicit capital convention is retained transparently; terminal FCFF growth differs slightly from stable revenue growth. Later gross-capital components are unmodeled, not zero.

bottom line
bottom line · 5 records
  1. The existing 87,209.56 cumulative economic FCFF deficit peaks after year 2; it is not an annual cash-financing requirement.
  2. The latest CY2026 gross cash capex guide is 195,000–205,000. The rolling year ending June2027 includes the higher 2027 spend profile, so 196,181 of net reinvestment is plausible; neither an error nor proof of financing distress can be inferred from comparison with the calendar guide.
  3. Reported TTM cash FCF 53,273 becomes a normalized, SBC-expensed, PPE-only FCFF proxy of -4,139.16 at a 22% operating tax rate. Working-capital tax movements are explicitly removed in the bridge.
  4. Rapid D&A catch-up can eventually reduce net reinvestment, but the latest guide, 122,814 of assets not yet in service and 707,000 of multiyear purchase commitments do not support assuming immediate investment normalization.
  5. Cash and current debt securities total 155,411 before liquidity buffers and constraints, versus headline cash/current marketables of 242,474. Current equity investments must not be treated as cash.

bridge method
bridge method · 9 fields
CFO identity
NI + PP&E depreciation + SBC + deferred tax adjustment - securities gains + other noncash + non-tax WC cash effect + income-tax WC cash effect
normalized PPE proxy

equivalent identity

caution
H1 and TTM cash-flow-implied amounts are algebraic all-items approximations, not separately disclosed cash taxes. They include taxes on nonoperating results, settlements, temporary differences and rounding/classification effects.
limits
PPE-only proxy strips the entire other noncash line for exact reproducibility. Restore independently verified operating amortization and appropriate operating noncash charges; do not treat this stripped residual as precise final FCFF. H1 intangible amortization 545 yields -25,109.52 before financing-lease asset adjustments. FY2025 full intangible amortization was not separately identified in this review, so no unsupported TTM estimate is added.
interest
H1 interest expense 1,811 and interest income 2,811 are in OI&E, which this bridge removes together with other nonoperating amounts. Adding after-tax interest again would double count. The 628 of H1 capitalized interest requires a consistent capex/financing convention; do not assume accrued interest equals cash interest paid.
sbc
Retain SBC in EBIT/NOPAT and do not add it back to economic FCFF. Add the actual noncash SBC cash-flow adjustment only in the separate cash-funding bridge. Forecast employee equity dilution or its replacement cost consistently; do not charge the same SBC cost again through both an expense-retained valuation and a full replacement-cost/share-dilution penalty.
WC
H1 non-tax WC cash consumption is 21,406, including inventory 7,739 and receivables 6,904; tax WC is a separate +8,304. Never combine a normal WC forecast with a second customer-prepayment benefit already inside that forecast.

classification
Analytical scenario ranges anchored to guide, investment backlog, depreciation policy and observed WC. They are not management forecasts or confidence intervals; extreme component bounds need not occur together.
range rationale
June2027 gross capex range assumes roughly 111–141bn H1 2027 at the matching guide endpoints. June2028 permits continuing 2027 ramp and June2029 allows stabilization or another expansion. D&A rises as the 122.8bn construction/installation pipeline and new cohorts enter service. Inventory/receivables keep WC a possible cash use; customer backlog itself supplies no cash.
normalization conditions
normalization conditions · 5 records
  1. Use 2027/2028 physical deliveries and cohort depreciation to decide whether 2029 capex stabilizes; do not automatically fade cash capex when revenue growth fades.
  2. Test supplier-credit unwind, TPU inventory-to-revenue conversion, leased capacity cost and acquired-intangible amortization separately.
  3. D&A ranges are intended as total operating D&A, including verified intangible amortization and finance-lease asset depreciation. Reconcile the finance-lease amortization disclosure to modeled PP&E depreciation before any separate addback; include it once.
  4. After June2029, transition asset cohorts and reinvestment over several years. Do not jump from explicit capital spending to a terminal sales/capital ratio; satisfy terminal net reinvestment = growth/ROIC*NOPAT.
  5. 22% tax and original revenue/NOPAT are sensitivities. Higher depreciation, temporary third-party capacity and TPU hardware mix must also be tested through margins; preserving margins while changing D&A is not an integrated forecast.

interpretation
Original first-year net reinvestment lies inside the explicit range. There is no source-supported reason to force it downward purely to eliminate a deficit. The mechanically linked sales/capital path omits D&A, supplier financing, leases and cash taxes needed to explain cash funding.
forward cash funding identity
forward cash funding identity · 6 records
  1. Start with economic FCFF with SBC expensed and operating taxes normalized.
  2. Add back the noncash SBC cash-flow adjustment only to measure cash available; separately recognize the employee equity claim consistently in valuation.
  3. Add actual temporary operating tax savings (or subtract reversals), and bridge cash nonoperating receipts and cash interest; do not use unrealized securities/derivative gains as funding.
  4. If economic reinvestment included financed lease assets or accrued capital-payable increases, add matching financing sources, then deduct actual principal/prepayments or supplier settlements only once. If using cash capex, do not add supplier financing again.
  5. Deduct strategic equity/customer financing, acquisitions, dividends, employee award withholding, debt maturities and any other cash commitments excluded from operating FCFF.
  6. Then apply existing liquid assets above an explicit buffer and new net debt/equity financing. This required-financing balance is distinct from cumulative economic FCFF.

treatment
Schedule commitments in the appropriate capex, inventory/COGS, rent, financing or contingent-loss line. Do not subtract notional commitments as extra debt on top of forecast spending. The 20bn contingent funding is inside 21.9bn VIE commitments, not additive. Existing lease VIE exposures are already in lease totals. rules
rules · 4 records
  1. RPO includes unbilled future invoices and is not a funding balance.
  2. Deferred revenue is received or due before performance, and can be refundable; the balance is not necessarily all cash already collected.
  3. Use only actual deferred-revenue cash movement once, via WC; do not also net backlog/customer advances against gross capex.
  4. Customer financing investments and credit backstops consume or risk funding; they are not independent evidence that recognized revenue is cash-funded.
completion
No pre-existing files overwritten; standalone analysis only. No valuation, target price, share-price calibration or automatic assumption revision.

Future ATM proceeds offset a cash funding use only when actually issued and are financing with dilution. They do not reduce SBC expense, make stock-award withholding disappear, or add June cash. residual gates

  1. Integrate D&A, TPU hardware inventory/COGS, energy and third-party capacity costs with EBIT before treating overlay as a fully integrated forecast.

rationale
rationale · 10 fields
growth
18% is below the latest 24% quarter and above FY2025 growth of 15.1%. Cloud expansion supports the uplift, while Search scale and competitive substitution force a deceleration.
target Margin
30% is below 33.1% TTM. Search monetization and Cloud scale are offset by AI compute costs, traffic acquisition and investment in new products.
tax
22% normalizes operating taxes above recent effective rates; very large non-operating equity gains make consolidated pretax-income tax ratios unsuitable as a direct operating forecast.
sales Capital
0.7x requires $1.43 of net investment per extra $1 of revenue. The current AI buildout warrants much more capital than the historic search-only model.
terminal ROIC
15% retains valuable distribution and software assets but reduces returns as competition and infrastructure intensity rise.
wacc
10.0% nominal USD is a rounded model estimate. Assumed beta 1.1, 5% target debt and a 0.8-point debt spread reflect strong core cash flow plus search-transition and regulatory exposure.
terminal Growth
2.5% nominal USD is a mature-state assumption with limited real expansion, well below the high-growth starting rate and the discount rate; it is not a company forecast.
years
10 years is the common model horizon so company economics can be compared; rates and margins fade over this period. The number is a modeling convention, not a source fact.
other Claims
0 means no additional user-entered claim beyond the separate explicit current claims model. Do not enter the same modeled claims again. The separate source-dated current claims model explicitly allocates mandatory preferred dilution/dividends, finance leases and noncontrolling claims, and adds a gross noncurrent-investment carrying proxy. Capped-call recovery, investment realization taxes and employee awards remain incomplete.
other Assets
0 means no additional user-entered asset beyond the separate explicit current claims model. Alphabet already includes a gross noncurrent-investment proxy in that bridge; never add it again. No zero is proof of absence.

priority
Senior to all three common classes; A and B rank equally; junior to indebtedness and any future senior stock. Liquidation preference plus accumulated unpaid dividends. No participation in residual assets after payment.
redemption
No issuer redemption or sinking fund. Ordinary holder early conversion uses the minimum rate, subject to adjustments.
voting
Preferred generally nonvoting, with protective/nonpayment exceptions. Common A has 1 vote, B 10 votes, C no vote except legally required. A/B/C economic dividend and liquidation rights are otherwise equal. Valuation does not price voting premiums.
mandatory Conversion Expected Date
2029-05-15
mandatory Conversion Date Rule
Second business day after the last trading day of the final averaging period; date can shift under contractual market-disruption rules.
applicable Market Value Rule
Arithmetic average of daily VWAP over 20 consecutive trading days beginning with the 21st scheduled trading day immediately preceding May 15, 2029. Each class uses its own future average.

default Treatment
No future capped-call asset or share offset is assumed; historical premium is already in June cash/equity and is never charged again. Zero future recovery is a conservative scenario assumption, not a finding that the options have no value.
settlement
Issuer can elect cash settlement; otherwise generally common shares based on excess over strike, limited by cap. Counterparty risk applies.
sensitivity Formula Only
At an explicitly assumed common future settlement price P, gross economic share offset approximation = minimum underlying shares * max(0, min(P, cap) - strike) / P. This ignores detailed averaging and adjustments; do not present it as observed option fair value.

base Equation
E = EV + reported cash/current marketables + analyst other-asset values - reported debt - finance leases - NCI value - additional non-preferred claims. v = (E - preferred-dividend PV) / (12230 + incremental preferred conversion shares).
timing Rationale
Conversion occurs inside the ten-year forecast. A static fully diluted denominator allocates all residual present equity to eventual shares, with no separately modeled preconversion common payouts. It is a transparent approximation to actual timed conversion, not an exact preferred fair-value calculation. Do not discount the number of conversion shares.
timing Refinement
If A is the present value of total common distributions before conversion, a consistent payout refinement is A/12230 + (E - dividendPV - A)/(12230 + q), holding other capital structure assumptions fixed. The default assumes A=0 for this allocation; it does not predict Alphabet will cease common dividends.
max Dilution Caveat
Maximum contractual gross shares gives the lower positive value only with other inputs held fixed, cash-paid preferred dividends, unchanged conversion terms, and no cap-call recovery. It is not a universal economic lower bound.

    warning
    An entire preferred fair-value claim includes conversion rights and dividend rights; subtracting additional conversion dilution or the whole dividend PV would double-count.
investment Treatment
Current cash bridge already includes 87063 of marketable equity. Noncurrent investments 145587 may be added as an explicitly selected gross carrying-value proxy with separate editable haircuts. Neither their full book value nor a zero haircut is a fair-value conclusion.
investment Taxes
Gross asset proxy has no implied realization-tax allowance. Add an explicit analyst tax reserve if used. Total reported deferred tax liabilities 22819 cannot be assigned wholesale to these investments without evidence.
operating Lease Treatment
Keep operating lease expense in forecast operating profit; do not mechanically add operating lease liabilities as debt without restating operating profit and reinvestment consistently.
other Awards
Quarterly weighted-average diluted EPS shares already include some preferred conversion effects and cannot be combined with full preferred conversion shares. Use actual June common count; existing employee awards require their own separately documented treatment.
numeric Precision
Retain calculation precision internally, but display valuation in sensible rounded dollars, not as exact security fair value. NCI/common counts and some dividends are rounded filing facts.

treatment
Known later financing is excluded from the June 30 balance-date valuation. Do not add only the new debt while retaining June cash; a current October value requires a complete cash/debt/capex and security roll-forward.
research Scope
Checked the available current SEC submissions listing and the August 10 closing 8-K. This is not a certification of every change through October 17 or a current quote.
double Counting Checks
double Counting Checks · 7 records
  1. Never subtract preferred carrying balance or liquidation principal in conversion mode.
  2. Never add full preferred dilution to an entire market-valued preferred claim deduction.
  3. Never add June preferred financing proceeds or charge June capped-call premium again.
  4. Never add RNCI 824 separately from NCI 7100.
  5. Never add current marketable equity 87063 again; it is within cash/current marketables 242474.
  6. Never combine aggregate diluted EPS shares with full conversion shares.
  7. Do not add all reported deferred taxes or operating lease debt mechanically.
limitations
limitations · 4 records
  1. No current GOOG, GOOGL, GOOGM or GOOGN quote was used or fabricated.
  2. These scenarios resolve the mandatory preferred mechanics sufficiently for a conditional educational valuation; they do not certify complete fair market value.
  3. Valuation uses June 30 balances and a forward forecast; October review date is not an October balance-sheet measurement.
  4. Potential taxation, security restrictions, employee awards and uncommenced infrastructure commitments remain explicit modeling limitations.
